title: Inu x Boku SS Marks 15 Years With New Artwork and a Japanese Rerun
excerpt:
The supernatural romance anime has unveiled a new anniversary illustration and refreshed website.
A Japanese television rerun is planned for January 2027, but no new season has been announced.
seo_title: Inu x Boku SS Anniversary Artwork and 2027 Rerun
seo_description: Inu x Boku SS celebrates its 15th anniversary with new character art, a Japanese rerun and merchandise, not a confirmed sequel.
body_md:
Inu x Boku SS is returning to the spotlight for its fifteenth anniversary, although not through a newly commissioned season. The official anime website has been refreshed, and character designer and chief animation director Haruko Iizuka has created a commemorative illustration bringing the central cast back together. The celebration highlights the enduring audience for a supernatural romance whose original television run ended many years ago.

Ririchiyo Shirakiin and her devoted bodyguard Soshi Miketsukami anchor the new artwork. Other residents of Maison de Ayakashi and their attendants appear around them, including Nobara Yukinokouji, Renshou Sorinozuka, Banri Watanuki, Zange Natsume, Karuta Roromiya and Kagerou Shoukiin. Formal clothing, presents and party decorations establish the celebratory tone. The illustration is an anniversary commission rather than evidence of a sequel entering production.

The most substantial programming announcement is a Japanese rebroadcast scheduled to begin in January 2027. The report does not specify an exact premiere day or a new international distribution arrangement. Before the rerun, a stage event at Japan's Kitakyushu Pop Culture Festival will feature Rina Hidaka, who voices Ririchiyo, and Yoko Hikasa, the voice of Nobara. These appearances offer fans another chance to engage with performers associated with the original adaptation.

Adapted by David Production from Cocoa Fujiwara's manga, the series follows Ririchiyo, a young heiress living in a residence populated by people with supernatural connections. Her evolving relationship with Soshi, a fiercely loyal protector, provides the emotional foundation. The wider ensemble and the show's mixture of romantic tension and low-key fantasy distinguish it from more conventional school romances.

The television adaptation ran for twelve episodes and covered roughly four volumes of the eleven-volume manga. Consequently, much of the source material's later, darker storytelling never reached the screen. The manga has exceeded 5.1 million copies in circulation, while its ninth volume reportedly sold more than 200,000 copies in its first week, illustrating the franchise's sustained appeal beyond the anime's brief run.

Anniversary merchandise and planned Good Smile Company Nendoroid figures add to the celebrations. However, neither a second season nor a continuation adapting the remaining manga chapters has been formally confirmed. For now, the confirmed developments are new artwork, fan events, products and a January 2027 rerun in Japan.
